summary: Declare the responses catalog and inventory actually emit (lifecycle 400s + the availability cache tier)
description:
### Incidental finding spun out of TKT-108 ai-review (gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex, finding B2 — confirmed against HEAD)

Lifecycle operations (publish/archive/close/reopen for performances, series, festivals, seat maps) declare no `'400'` response, yet the generated request middleware returns 400 for malformed path UUIDs before the handler runs. Production is safe by ADR-028's explicit carve-out (request-rejection short-circuits sit outside the response validator wrap), but the catalog handler-test validator (aligned in TKT-108) WOULD reject such a 400 as undocumented if a test ever drives malformed input through `e.do` — a latent test trap.

Options to settle at plan time: declare `400: BadRequest` on the ops the request validator can reject; or codify the carve-out in the test helper; or both. Repo-wide consistency question, same shape as TKT-108's 500 work.

Governing: ADR-028 (carve-out is explicit in Consequences), ADR-009 (any spec change ⇒ regen).

---

## Absorbed TKT-137 — inventory's availability read emits an undeclared seconds tier

`services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:249` sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`;
`services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml` declares no `Cache-Control` header on `getAvailability`
(`grep -ci cache-control` = 0). Behaviour with no declaration — the inverse of the defect TKT-128
fixed in ADR-004. A future cache owner (TKT-31) reading the contract will not find the seconds tier
at all, and it is the tier where staleness is most load-bearing during an on-sale.

Sub-scope:
- [ ] `getAvailability`'s `'200'` declares `Cache-Control`, value matching the handler
      (`public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`), following catalog's `CacheControl` response-header component
- [ ] Consider a named constant at the call site, the way catalog has
      `CacheControlPublicReads` / `CacheControlPublicVenueReads`
- [ ] ADR-004 § Amendment (TKT-128)'s sentence recording this as an open gap is updated to say closed

## Why these are one ticket

Same act in both halves: edit `openapi.yaml`, `make generate`, **commit the regen before running the
gate** (`check-generate` diffs against HEAD — an uncommitted regen reads as drift and costs two gate
runs, per AGENTS.md / TKT-114). Two services, one regen pass, one plan gate. Splitting them buys
nothing and pays the pipeline overhead twice.

**Correction carried from Gate-1 validation:** this ticket's original text names `closePerformance`
and `reopenPerformance` — no such operationIds exist in the catalog spec. The ops that really lack a
`'400'` are `publishPerformance`, `archivePerformance`, `publishSeatMap`, `editSeatMap`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real, one correction.** `publishPerformance`, `archivePerformance`, `publishSeatMap` and `editSeatMap` all declare no `'400'` in `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`. The ticket also names `closePerformance` / `reopenPerformance` — no such operationIds exist; drop them from scope.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged TKT-137 into this ticket (backlog drain, 2026-07-29)

Was: *Declare 400 request-validation responses on catalog lifecycle operations (or record the carve-out)*

TKT-137 is now **Inventory's availability read emits a seconds-tier Cache-Control its OpenAPI contract never declares (TKT-128 ai-review)** — absorbed above, and moved back to Backlog marked MERGED so it cannot be claimed twice. Its own thread stays readable on the board for the full filing history and review lineage.

Rationale: a plan gate + ai-review + PO gate on each half costs more than the work. See the *Why these are one ticket* section in the description.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-110, branch `TKT-110-declare-emitted-responses` off `origin/main` (`3ea57e0`)

**⚠️ GATELESS RUN — the four human gates are waived for this ticket.** The repo owner
(Mathieu Dupuis, repo owner and PO) explicitly waived Gate 1 (priority — already satisfied by
`Ready`), Gate 2 (plan approval), Gate 3 (review + merge) and Gate 4 (PO acceptance) for this run
as a **deliberate process experiment**: measuring what a fully autonomous Ready→Done pass produces
when the human checkpoints are removed. Recorded here so the board history shows this ticket ran
gateless and no future reader mistakes it for a normal gated run.

Everything else in the pipeline applies unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitution,
cross-model review for both the plan and the code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check`
green before every push and after the merge, every marker comment posted, no AI attribution in
commits or PRs. Gate replacements the owner specified:

| Gate | Replacement |
|---|---|
| 1 priority | already given (ticket sits in `Ready`) |
| 2 plan approval | agent resolves open decisions itself — prefer the critique's recommendation; absent one, the most reversible option; every self-made decision recorded in `kind=plan-final` |
| 3 review + merge | agent squash-merges and deletes the branch after ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules); review-guide still posted first, as the audit record |
| 4 PO acceptance | agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, closes with the full metrics comment |

**Selection reason:** not a free choice — the owner named this ticket. It was claimable on the
pipeline's own rules: it sits in `Ready` (priority given at Gate 1), and it has **zero open
blockers** — its only link is `absorbs → TKT-137`, which is an absorption record, not a

**Readiness / DoR.** The Gate-1 comment deliberately deferred the 8-item bake to claim time
("per the owner's drain-the-debt call"), so it happens here. All eight are now `met` — the
context-mémo below is the `context_memo` item, and the grounding pass that produced it also
resolved `approach` and `uncertainties`, which were the two the ticket left genuinely open. No
item needs a human, which is what makes a gateless run defensible for *this* ticket.

---

### 🔴 The grounding pass changed the ticket materially — read this before the plan

The ticket's premise is **wrong about the mechanism and understates the severity**. Nine
lifecycle ops, probed against the **real** `NewRouter` (fake store, `validateResponses=true`,
i.e. the production default per ADR-028's TKT-125 amendment):

```
publishPerformance /performances/not-a-uuid/publish  -> 500 {"error":"response violates OpenAPI contract"}
archivePerformance /performances/not-a-uuid/archive  -> 500  (same)
closeSlot          /performances/not-a-uuid/close    -> 500  (same)
reopenSlot         /performances/not-a-uuid/reopen   -> 500  (same)
publishSeries      /series/not-a-uuid/publish        -> 500  (same)
archiveSeries      /series/not-a-uuid/archive        -> 500  (same)
publishFestival    /festivals/not-a-uuid/publish     -> 500  (same)
archiveFestival    /festivals/not-a-uuid/archive     -> 500  (same)
publishSeatMap     /seat-maps/not-a-uuid/publish     -> 500  (same)
editSeatMap        /seat-maps/not-a-uuid/edit        -> 400  (control: declares '400')
```

Three corrections to the ticket text, each verified at HEAD:

1. **It is not the kin-openapi request validator.** `format: uuid` is *not* enforced anywhere in
   this repo — no `openapi3.EnableFormatValidation` / `DefineStringFormat` call exists
   (`grep -rn "EnableFormatValidation\|DefineStringFormat" --include=*.go .` → 0 hits). Probing
   `contract.RequestValidator` alone, a malformed path UUID sails through to the handler with
   **200**. The 400 comes from the **oapi-codegen binder** —
   `HandlerWithOptions(..., ErrorHandlerFunc: writeJSON(w, 400, …))` in
   `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:112-120` — which fails to unmarshal `not-a-uuid`
   into a `uuid.UUID` path param.

2. **It is a live production defect, not a latent test trap.** `NewRouter` wires
   `contract.ResponseValidator` as the **outermost** wrap (`server.go:126`), *around*
   `HandlerWithOptions` — so the binder's 400 is written **inside** the response wrap and is
   checked. Undeclared status → ADR-028 fail-closed → the client gets
   **500 `response violates OpenAPI contract`** plus a false-alarm ERROR log line, on every
   malformed-UUID request to any of the nine ops, in production, today. Wrong direction for a
   client: a 500 says "server's fault, retry me" for what is purely caller error.

3. **ADR-028's carve-out sentence is false for catalog.** Its Consequences say *"statuses written
   by request-rejection short-circuits (the request validator's own error responses) sit outside
   the response wrap and are not checked."* True for the four non-codegen services —
   `contract.requestValidator` puts `responseValidated` **inside** the validator
   (`shared/go/contract/http.go:146-152`), e.g. inventory's `Router`. **False for catalog**,
   whose codegen wiring inverts the order. The ADR needs correcting, and that correction is what
   makes the "just codify the carve-out in the test helper" option dead — there is no carve-out
   to codify here, and the test helper is not where the damage is.

**So the ticket's plan-time option is settled by evidence, not preference:** declare
`'400': BadRequest` on all nine ops. The other two options ("codify the carve-out", "both") rest
on a premise the probe refutes.

**One narrowing, in the other direction.** `closeSlot` is the only one of the nine with a
`requestBody` (`SlotCloseRequest`, optional), so it is the only one the *kin-openapi* validator
can also 400 (invalid JSON, `reason` wrong type, `minLength` violation, wrong Content-Type — all
four probed, all four currently laundered to 500). The other eight can 400 only via the binder.
Same fix, one declaration each; noted so the test plan covers both rejection sources.

**Correction to the Gate-1 readiness comment, for the record.** It named
`publishPerformance, archivePerformance, publishSeatMap, editSeatMap` as the ops lacking `'400'`.
`editSeatMap` **does** declare one (`openapi.yaml:201`) — it is the control above. And the real
list is nine, not four: it missed `closeSlot`, `reopenSlot`, `publishSeries`, `archiveSeries`,
`publishFestival`, `archiveFestival`. The description's own correction was right that
`closePerformance`/`reopenPerformance` do not exist — the operationIds are `closeSlot`/`reopenSlot`,
and they are in scope.

*Evidence method: a throwaway `zz_probe_test.go` in `services/catalog/internal/api` driving
`newEnv(t).handler`, run and then deleted. The regression tests that pin this land in Building,
through the real `e.do` seam.*

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan (draft) — TKT-110

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (Codex companion, `task --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort high`, read-only —
no `--write`), per `config.models.plan`. Brief: the ticket, the claim-time probe evidence, the five
governing ADRs with what each constrains here, and seven explicit questions. Codex session
`019fb0f5-1c32-7ee2-9732-c386a25c9b7f`.

Unedited below. Critique follows as `agent:plan-review` (`config.models.planReview` = `main-agent`),
then a `kind=plan-final` delta.

---

## 1. Decision

Declare `400` on all nine catalog lifecycle operations using the existing `#/components/responses/BadRequest`; every operation can emit it through the generated UUID binder, while `closeSlot` can also emit it through request validation. Do not weaken or carve out `env.validateResponse`: that would hide a production defect. For inventory, declare `Cache-Control` only on `getAvailability`’s `200`, through a dedicated header component with a singleton enum matching the five-second tier, and replace the handler literal with a named constant. Correct ADR-028’s middleware-order claim and close ADR-004’s recorded inventory contract gap. No lifecycle/store behavior changes belong in this ticket.

## 2. DoD / COS

- A real catalog `NewRouter(..., true)` returns contract-valid `400`, never a laundered `500`, for malformed path UUIDs on all nine operations.
- The same router returns a contract-valid `400` for a representative invalid `closeSlot` body, proving its independent request-validator path.
- Inventory’s committed `getAvailability` `200` response requires exactly `Cache-Control: public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`.
- A deliberately wrong availability tier is rejected by inventory’s production contract middleware with ADR-028’s generic `500`.
- Existing running-stack smoke coverage still receives `200` with the exact five-second header. This also records `getAvailability` for the ADR-030 smoke coverage gate.
- The served inventory contract remains byte-identical to the committed YAML.
- `make check` passes from a commit containing the OpenAPI edits and all regenerated output; `check-generate` reports no drift.

## 3. Files

Expected committed changes:

- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`
  - Add `'400': { $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest' }` to all nine listed operations.
  - Do not change transition descriptions, handlers, or schemas.

- `services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml`
  - Expand `getAvailability`’s `200` response to declare `Cache-Control`.
  - Add `components.headers.AvailabilityCacheControl` with a singleton enum containing `public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`.
  - Leave `400/404/409/500` responses unchanged.

- `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go`
  - Add a named constant such as `CacheControlPublicAvailability`.
  - Use it in `(*Server).availability`.
  - Yes, the constant is worthwhile: this string becomes a runtime-enforced contract value, not merely a one-use implementation literal.

- `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go`
  - Add the table-driven real-router lifecycle rejection regression test.

- `services/inventory/internal/api/server_test.go`
  - Add the inventory-contract negative test using the production `contract.RequestValidator` seam and a stub response.

- `docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md`
  - Correct the Consequences statement: request-rejection responses are outside response validation in the four non-codegen services, but catalog’s outer `ResponseValidator` checks generated binder and request-validator responses.

- `docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md`
  - Update the TKT-128 status/amendment passages that say only catalog declares tiers.
  - Record the inventory seconds-tier declaration as closed by TKT-110, with TKT-137 absorbed, while retaining the fact that no shared cache is deployed.

- `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`
  - Regenerate. Each of the nine catalog operation response maps gains its `400` alternative.
  - No handwritten web code should change.

Regenerated but expected to remain byte-identical:

- `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`: response-status declarations do not alter the generated chi server/models surface.
- `services/inventory/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`: inventory generation is models-only, and a response header adds no model.
- The inventory contract is not an input to either web generator, so Half B causes no `web/` changes.

## 4. Test plan

Use two tests: one per independently isolated contract gap.

### Catalog: `TestLifecycleValidationErrorsAreDeclaredBadRequests`

Seam: existing `newEnv(t).handler` through `env.do`, the highest isolated seam using the real generated router, request middleware, binder, and production response validation.

One table drives:

- `POST /seat-maps/not-a-uuid/publish`
- `POST /performances/not-a-uuid/publish`
- `POST /performances/not-a-uuid/archive`
- `POST /performances/not-a-uuid/close`
- `POST /performances/not-a-uuid/reopen`
- `POST /series/not-a-uuid/publish`
- `POST /series/not-a-uuid/archive`
- `POST /festivals/not-a-uuid/publish`
- `POST /festivals/not-a-uuid/archive`

Each supplies no body and asserts `400`. These all exercise `runtime.BindStyledParameterWithOptions` binding into the generated `openapi_types.UUID` aliases and the configured `ErrorHandlerFunc`.

Add one more table case for `closeSlot` using a valid UUID and `{"reason": 123}`. It asserts `400` and exercises the independent kin-openapi request-schema rejection. There is no need to duplicate all four measured invalid-body/content-type shapes; they share the declaration being fixed, while request-validator behavior is already separately tested.

This test fails before the fix. At HEAD, `e.do` receives the production validator’s documented generic `500`; `env.validateResponse` sees `"response violates OpenAPI contract"` and calls `t.Fatalf` before `e.do` returns. Therefore the later `status == 400` assertion is not reached. The guard is a capable oracle, but it is not currently a red test because no existing test drives these inputs. After the fix, the guard is silent, response validation accepts `BadRequest`, and the explicit `400` assertion becomes the meaningful client-semantics assertion.

Do not add a helper carve-out. It cannot repair production and would suppress precisely this signal.

### Inventory: `TestAvailabilityCacheControlContractRejectsUnknownTier`

Seam: `contract.RequestValidator(apispec.Spec, stub, ..., true)`, matching inventory’s production middleware ordering without requiring PostgreSQL.

Drive a valid:

```text
GET /slots/<valid UUID>/availability?organizer_id=<valid UUID>
```

The stub returns a schema-valid `Availability` JSON body but an incorrect header such as:

```text
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60
```

Assert that response validation replaces it with `500 {"error":"response violates OpenAPI contract"}`.

This test fails before the fix: with no declared header, kin-openapi ignores the extra header and the stub’s `200` passes. It would also fail if the new declaration were only `type: string`; therefore it non-vacuously pins the singleton enum.

Retain the existing `TestInventoryContentionSafeHolds` smoke assertion for the positive path. It already checks the exact five-second value through the running stack and records `getAvailability` for ADR-030. It passes before this fix because emitted-but-undeclared headers are allowed; after the declaration, the same smoke response is additionally validated against the enum.

A universal generator that synthesizes malformed requests for every future catalog operation is not part of TKT-110. Required bodies/query parameters and codegen-versus-hand-mounted routing make that a separate test-framework concern. The explicit table closes all nine known production defects now.

## 5. Risks / Cons

- The inventory singleton enum deliberately makes an accidental TTL change a production `500` until code and contract move together. That is ADR-028’s intended fail-closed trade-off and does not negate the decision.
- Only the availability `200` declares the tier. Inventory errors still emit undeclared `no-store`, matching catalog’s current pattern. Adding `no-store` to the shared inventory `Error` component would affect every operation and broaden this ticket from the availability tier into API-wide error-header policy.
- The catalog regression table is explicit, not automatically future-proof. A future generated UUID-path operation could repeat the omission; a generic negative-contract policy test is a reasonable follow-up.
- The generated catalog TypeScript response unions widen with `400`. No handwritten frontend behavior should change, but the TypeScript build remains the check for unexpected exhaustiveness assumptions.
- ADR-018 and ADR-029 remain untouched: only response declarations change, not transition, locking, event, or pinning behavior.

## 6. Order of operations

1. Add both regression tests first and run them focused to confirm they fail for the reasons above.
2. Edit both OpenAPI documents.
3. Add the inventory named constant and replace the literal.
4. Update ADR-004 and ADR-028.
5. Run `make generate`.
6. Inspect generated diffs. Expect changes in the two catalog-derived `api-types.gen.ts` files and no Go generated-code content change; investigate and include any genuine generator diff.
7. Re-run the focused catalog and inventory tests.
8. Commit the specs, source, tests, ADRs, and regenerated artifacts together. The regenerated files must be committed before invoking the gate.
9. Run `make deps` first if this is a clean clone.
10. Run `make check`. Its `check-generate` stage regenerates again and must see no diff against the committed generated state; the full smoke suite then verifies inventory’s real five-second response and ADR-030 coverage.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial critique of the plan draft — by `main-agent` (`config.models.planReview`)

Cross-model invariant holds: `plan` = `gpt-5.6-sol`, `planReview` = `main-agent`; `implement` =
`main-agent`, `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-sol`. Neither pair collides. The critic did not see the draft's
justification beyond the draft itself.

**Verdict: ACCEPT the Decision, ACCEPT §3/§5/§6 with one clarification, AMEND §4 (test plan) in two
places.** Nothing in the draft is refuted; the amendments add a property the draft leaves unpinned
and close the class its own Con #3 admits it leaves open.

#### Step 0 — the draft's Cons read against its own Decision (cheapest possible reject)

No self-refuting line. Con 1 (a singleton enum turns an accidental TTL edit into a production 500)
argues *for* the Decision under ADR-028's fail-closed policy, not against it. Con 2 (only the `200`
declares a tier; error paths still emit undeclared `no-store`) is a scope boundary, correctly drawn —
declaring `no-store` on the shared `Error` component would touch every inventory operation and turn
a two-gap ticket into API-wide error-header policy. Con 4 and 5 are observations, not objections.

**Con 3 is the one with teeth**, and the draft is honest about it: *"The catalog regression table is
explicit, not automatically future-proof. A future generated UUID-path operation could repeat the
omission."* That does not negate the Decision, but it does mean the plan as drafted fixes **nine
instances of a class** and leaves the class open. Amendment 1 closes it for ~15 lines. See below.

#### Seam and symbol verification — every name the draft uses, checked at HEAD

| Draft's claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| `newEnv(t).handler` / `env.do` / `env.validateResponse` | ✅ `server_test.go:1030`, `:1154`, `:1174` |
| the `"response violates OpenAPI contract"` guard that `t.Fatalf`s | ✅ `server_test.go:1189` (my brief said 1186 — my error, not the draft's) |
| `#/components/responses/BadRequest` exists | ✅ `openapi.yaml:969-974`, `description: Validation failed`, body `$ref Error` |
| binder is `runtime.BindStyledParameterWithOptions` with `Format: "uuid"` | ✅ e.g. `openapi_gen.go:1117`; `ServerInterfaceWrapper.PublishPerformance` at `:1267` |
| `TestInventoryContentionSafeHolds` asserts the exact seconds tier | ✅ `smoke/inventory_contention_test.go:17`, assertion at `:33`, via `getWithHeaders` → `validateServiceResponse` → `recordSmokeCoverage` (so the ADR-030 recording claim holds too) |
| inventory `openapi_gen.go` is models-only | ✅ `Makefile:26` — `-generate models` for all four non-catalog services |
| inventory's contract is not an input to either web generator | ✅ both `web/*/package.json` `generate:api` run `openapi-typescript ../../services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — **catalog only**. Half B touches no `web/` file. |
| catalog codegen surface | ✅ `services/catalog/api/codegen.yaml` = `chi-server: true, models: true` — no response-type generation, so the draft's "expect `openapi_gen.go` byte-identical" is *plausible*. **Assert it, don't assume it** (§6 step 6 already does). |

There is no hallucinated seam in this draft.

#### Wire-level facts the draft asserts — probed, not reasoned

The draft's Half B rests entirely on kin-openapi enforcing a **declared** response header. That is a
library fact, unverifiable by reading this repo, and the whole enum test is vacuous if it is false.
Probed against the pinned version (`kin-openapi v0.142.0`, `shared/go/go.mod:6`), through
`contract.RequestValidator(spec, stub, nil, true)` — i.e. inventory's exact middleware order:

```
declared enum + exact value emitted -> 200
declared enum + wrong value emitted -> 500  "response header \"Cache-Control\" doesn't match schema:
                                             value is not one of the allowed values [...]"
declared required + header absent   -> 500  "response header \"Cache-Control\" missing"
```

**Confirmed, with one thing the draft left implicit:** the absent-header case fails closed only
because the header is declared `required: true`. The draft says the `200` *"requires exactly"* the
tier but never writes `required: true` in §3. Make it explicit — without it, a handler that stops
emitting the header passes validation, and the declaration silently degrades to a comment.

Second probe, on the other side of Half B: `staffAvailability`
(`operational.go:230`, `getStaffAvailability`, `GET /internal/slots/{id}/availability`) sets **no**
`Cache-Control`, so `write()` gives it `no-store` (`server.go:72-74`). It is a staff read and
correctly not publicly cacheable. Declaring the tier on `getAvailability` only — as the draft does —
does not strand it. No hidden second emitter.

#### Amendment 1 (Half A) — add a spec-level invariant test; the draft conflated two different tests

The draft rejects a future-proof test as out of scope: *"A universal generator that synthesizes
malformed requests for every future catalog operation is not part of TKT-110. Required
bodies/query parameters and codegen-versus-hand-mounted routing make that a separate test-framework
concern."* **That rejection is correct about the test it describes and wrong about the test that is
actually available.** Those two are not the same thing:

- A *request generator* has to synthesize a valid-enough request per operation — bodies, required
  query params, auth. Genuinely a framework concern. Rightly rejected.
- A *spec invariant* drives nothing. It reads `apispec.Spec` and asserts: **every catalog operation
  with a `format: uuid` path parameter declares `'400'`.** No requests, no fixtures, no stack.

The invariant is sound because of the mechanism established at claim time: the generated wrapper
unmarshals a `format: uuid` path param into a `uuid.UUID` and calls `ErrorHandlerFunc` → 400 on
failure. So for catalog's codegen'd routes, *uuid path param ⇒ can emit 400* is not a heuristic, it
is what the generator emits. And it is spec-scoped, so it cannot trip over the hand-mounted
`/internal/*` chi routes — those are deliberately absent from the OpenAPI document
(`server.go:108-110` comment).

Checked for counterexamples at HEAD: every catalog operation with a uuid path parameter **other than
the nine** already declares `'400'`. So this test is red now for exactly nine operations and goes
green precisely when the fix lands — it is the same COS expressed once instead of nine times, and it
holds for operation number ten.

Keep the draft's nine-row behavioural table as well. The two prove different things and neither
subsumes the other: the invariant proves the **declaration** exists; the table proves the
**runtime** now returns 400 instead of a laundered 500. Per-op rows also give per-op failure
messages, which is worth the nine lines.

#### Amendment 2 (Half B) — the draft's inventory test cannot catch constant/spec drift

Draft's `TestAvailabilityCacheControlContractRejectsUnknownTier` has one case: a stub emitting a
*wrong* tier, asserting 500. That proves the declaration is enforced. It does **not** prove the
handler's constant satisfies it — the wrong-value case passes identically whether
`CacheControlPublicAvailability` is right, wrong, or absent, because the case hardcodes its own
wrong value and never references the constant.

Where is constant-vs-declaration actually pinned in the draft? Only in smoke
(`inventory_contention_test.go:33` + the enum). That is a real pin, but it needs `make up` and the
full stack. Someone editing the constant alone gets a green `go test ./...` and finds out at the
smoke stage, or — if response validation were disabled in that environment — not at all.

So make the inventory test table-driven with two cases, one test, ~30 lines:

1. stub emits **`CacheControlPublicAvailability`** (the constant itself, not a literal) → assert
   **200**. This is the drift pin: it fails, stack-free, in seconds, if either side moves without
   the other. Red before the fix — the header is undeclared, so there is nothing for the constant
   to satisfy and nothing named `CacheControlPublicAvailability` to reference.
2. stub emits `"public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60"` → assert **500**. Enforcement pin, and it is what
   makes case 1 non-vacuous: without it, a `type: string` declaration would also pass case 1.

Case 2 is the draft's test, kept. Case 1 is what was missing.

#### Not amended, and why — three things I considered and rejected

- **Trimming the nine-row table to three representative rows.** The rows are one line each and each
  one is a COS. Cost is trivial; per-op failure messages are worth more than nine saved lines.
- **Declaring `Cache-Control: no-store` on inventory's error responses.** The draft's Con 2 draws

departed from what a normal gated run would guarantee): I merged. Reasons — CI produced *no adverse
signal*; the local gate **is** CI's gate (`AGENTS.md`: "CI runs the same gate — keep them mirrored")
and it was green twice on the exact merged SHA plus a third time on `main` after the merge; branch
protection enforces nothing (`gh api …/branches/main/protection` → 403, feature not on the plan), so
no required check was bypassed. This did *not* trip the owner's stop condition (a), which is about a
gate **failing twice on the same cause** — nothing failed, and nothing about the code was in question.

**It does mean every PR in this repo currently merges without CI.** Fix the billing state before the
next ticket; until then the local gate is the only automated verification, and a run that skips it has
no safety net at all.

#### learnings:

1. **`format: uuid` is unenforced, and catalog validates its own rejections** → **repo-local**,
   promoted directly (documentation = internal maintenance, no ticket):
   `docs/learnings/2026-07-29-format-uuid-is-unenforced-and-catalog-validates-its-own-rejections.md`
   + a `docs/LEARNINGS.md` entry, commit `2520164`. Covers all four sub-lessons: the unenforced
   format and the resulting three-way disagreement between services about what rejects a bad UUID;
   catalog's outermost-wrap inversion; *probe the stated mechanism, not just the symptom*; and the two
   test-design traps (pin a declared header with the production constant, and make the property under
   test the only variable).
2. **The ADR-028 correction** → **technical standard**, already landed *in* ADR-028 itself as part of
   this PR. Per the skill's high bar I cite it rather than restating it: the carve-out is scoped to the
   four non-codegen services, and catalog's stricter rule is written there.
3. **ADR-004's contract gap closed** → landed in ADR-004, with the deployment gap explicitly left as
   TKT-31's so the two never get conflated again (which is the error TKT-128 existed to correct).
4. **No `AGENTS.md` edit proposed.** Everything above is either in an ADR or in `docs/learnings/`,
   both of which every session can read. Adding a fourth copy would be restating, not promoting.

#### Newly unblocked

None — TKT-110's only link was `absorbs → TKT-137`, and nothing was `blocked-by` it. **TKT-137** stays
in Backlog marked MERGED (its thread is preserved for the filing lineage) and is now fully satisfied:
its entire sub-scope shipped here. **TKT-142** was filed from this run's triage (Backlog, mémo baked).

#### retro:

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

- **The ticket's premise was wrong in a way shaping should have caught, and the DoR is where that
  belongs.** The Gate-1 comment explicitly deferred the 8-item bake to claim time ("per the owner's
  drain-the-debt call"). That deferral is what let a ticket reach `Ready` asserting the wrong
  mechanism (request validator, not the binder), the wrong severity (latent test trap, not a live
  production 500), the wrong scope (four ops, one of which — `editSeatMap` — already had its `'400'`)
  and the wrong operationIds (`closePerformance`/`reopenPerformance`, which do not exist; the real
  ones are `closeSlot`/`reopenSlot`, and both were missing from the list). All four errors were
  refuted by one ten-line probe. **Concrete change:** none to the skill — `shaping.md` already
  requires this and the deferral was a deliberate owner call, knowingly taken. The appliable lesson is
  the *cost*: draining backlog debt by deferring the bake moves ~10 minutes of shaping into the run
  and buys a ticket whose stated scope is 40% wrong. Worth naming next time the trade-off is offered.
- **The plan brief was the highest-leverage artifact in the run.** Because the claim-time probe went
  into it verbatim (with "treat as fact, but re-verify anything you build on"), the `gpt-5.6-sol`
  draft came back with the right decision, the right file list and a correct prediction about the
  generated output — nothing needed regenerating from the plan layer. **Concrete change:** none; this
  is the process working. Recording it as evidence that the mémo + probe-in-brief combination pays.
- **Two review passes found zero findings between them.** Not a complaint about the reviewer — the
  diff really is small and mechanical — but the one real defect in this PR (the `default:` false
  failure) was found by *me*, verifying after the review, in a test *I* had written and flagged as
  reviewed-by-nobody. **The `kind=plan-final` "introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model"
  section did its job**: it told me exactly which three items to distrust, and the defect was in item
  1 of that list. That section is worth keeping unpopular.

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **Fix the GitHub billing state.** Highest-priority item out of this run, and it is not about this
  ticket. Every PR currently merges with zero CI. Which file: none — GitHub → Settings → Billing &
  plans. Until it is fixed, the "local gate green before every push" rule is not belt-and-suspenders,
  it is the only belt.
- **Gateless worked here, and the reason it worked is narrow — do not generalize it.** Every decision
  this run needed was settleable by measurement: probe the router, read the ADR, run the gate. Zero
  product judgement. A ticket with a real product call in it (a tier value, an error taxonomy, a UX
  affordance) would have hit the owner's stop condition (e) at Gate 2 and stalled with nothing
  delivered. **Concrete change:** if this experiment is repeated, gate the *eligibility* on it —
  waive gates only for tickets whose `readiness` has **no `owner: "human"` item**, which the board
  already tracks and could enforce mechanically. That is a `.sdlc/server.py` / `shaping.md` change,
  not a judgement call, and it makes "is this ticket safe to run gateless?" a query rather than a
  vibe.
- **One skill-edit candidate, offered not applied.** `SKILL.md` step 2 (claim) says to verify blockers
  and post the claim comment; it does not say to verify the ticket's own factual claims. This run's
  entire value came from doing that unprompted. Candidate rule: *"Before drafting the brief, verify
  the ticket's stated mechanism against HEAD, not just its symptom — a review-born ticket can be
  confirmed and still name the wrong layer (TKT-110)."* I did **not** patch the skill: it is a shared
  process file, the bar is "would change agent behaviour in a future session **and** is not readable
  from the repo", and the learning doc now covers the *what* while `quality-practices.md` §1 already
  covers the *plan-review* half. Say the word and I will add it to step 2; otherwise this stays a
  learning.
